provenance.paper_title: UniversalRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Corpora of Diverse Modalities and Granularities

representation_paths.memory_component: video corpus held at two granularities (full-length videos and segmented short clips)

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 2.2 UniversalRAG; Sec. 3.1 Experimental Setup / Implementation Details
evidence.paraphrase: Videos from LVBench and the VideoRAG corpora are stored as full-length items and additionally segmented into short clips, forming two separate granularity-level corpora, each embedded with a vision encoder (InternVideo2 in v1, VLM2Vec-V2 in v5) into its own independent embedding space and read by cosine similarity.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.1 Implementation Details (v1 wording retained across versions)
evidence.paraphrase: 32 frames are uniformly sampled per video for both the retrieval and the generation stage, so the retrieved video is handed to the LVLM generator as decoded frames rather than as a caption; the stored perceptual source is therefore directly accessible downstream. Scripts (for videos) and captions (for images) enter only the ensemble similarity score used for retrieval, not as a substitute memory record.

representation_paths.memory_component: image corpus kept intact (MRAG-Bench / WebQA / InfoSeek images)

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 2.2 UniversalRAG; Sec. 3.1 Experimental Setup
evidence.paraphrase: Images are kept intact because they are inherently piecemeal, indexed in their own vision embedding space, and the retrieved image itself is supplied to the multimodal generator (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct / InternVL3.5-8B / Molmo2-4B), which consumes textual and visual inputs.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 2.2 / Sec. 2.3 Router Implementation Strategies
evidence.paraphrase: Access is gated by a per-query modality-and-granularity router that runs before retrieval and selects which corpus (none / paragraph / document / table / image / clip / video) to query, i.e. a planner-style routing step layered on top of within-corpus similarity search.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (arXiv HTML v5, cross-checked against v1 for implementation details): the text, table, image, clip and video corpora are built before deployment and thereafter only queried. Nothing is written back, merged, decayed or re-indexed at inference; the router is trained offline (or prompted zero-shot) and its parameters/prompt are fixed at deployment. Query-conditioned routing plus top-k similarity selection over fixed items is explicitly T1 under the guide. Highest tier T1.

primary_modality is a close call: v5 evaluates on three image benchmarks (MRAG-Bench, WebQA, InfoSeek) and three video benchmarks (LVBench, VideoRAG-Wiki, VideoRAG-Synth). video_streaming was chosen because the video corpus is the largest persistent perceptual store and is the one on which the paper's granularity contribution is actually instantiated (full-length video vs. segmented clip corpora); image is recorded as a secondary operative modality.

The v5 HTML does not spell out in its Method section whether retrieved video reaches the generator as frames or as a script. The 'uniformly sample 32 frames per video for both the retrieval and generation stages' statement comes from the v1 implementation details; source_accessibility=direct for the video path rests on that sentence plus the use of frame-consuming LVLM generators, and should be re-checked against the ACL camera-ready PDF.
